You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

The installed workspace skills are stale (horizon-inbox). Do not overwrite deliberate local edits automatically, but do not ignore the drift. Until it is reconciled: use the `lean-check` LSP loop before and after Lean edits; spawn and wait for a bounded native subagent on multi-file/multi-proof work; and dispatch `janitor` (`ground` fallback) for inbox/roadmap/task health warnings and before terminal completion.

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajcr-charts
Title: C9 chartLocus, the chart pair, and DAT-B/DAT-C coverage
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.c9b,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.chart-u,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b; inbox=I-0492,I-0494

BUILD THE CHART LAYER: chartLocus and the (f, hf) chart pair, then close DAT-B coverage/injectivity and DAT-C Sigma-charts. Roadmap AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus (with .c9b and .chart-u) plus dat-b and dat-c. C9 is the sole gate of DAT-B B-6 AND of the whole dat-glue assembly, so this is the second-highest-leverage lane in the project.

FOUR DELIVERABLES.

 (1) CHART-U(a)/(b) — THE CO-SIGNED BRICK, and start here because nothing in the tree implements it. chartLocus c lambda (w4-datc-worksheet.md section 3.3, CHART-U(a)) is a locus over a GENERAL TEST T indexed by a plus class lambda, and isOpen_chartLocus is CHART-U(b). Its node names three missing inputs — read them before writing. This is a genuine construction task, not a proof-hunting one, and it is developable PARAMETRICALLY, i.e. without waiting for the certificate lane.

 (2) C9a IS DONE, C9b IS THE DELIVERABLE PROPER. chartLocus is already DEFINED and OPEN at the parameter-space carrier level (the C9 split of 2026-07-26). What remains is f_c, the chart morphism, and the (f, hf) pair that pic0RepresentableByOfCharts (Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) consumes. HONEST GATE, corrected and adversarially verified: c9b is NOT merely divRep-gated — read its node for what the real gate is, and note it is developable parametrically ahead of CERT-Sigma.

 (3) DAT-B COVERAGE AND INJECTIVITY: every pic^0 point is Zariski-locally a chart point. Coverage-drop, separably-closed points, divisor-family field surjectivity, local chart openness and fibre-field invariance are ALL LANDED — what remains is B5/B6/chart-locus packaging, which is exactly what (1) and (2) unblock.

 (4) DAT-C SIGMA-CHARTS: C0-C5 are landed. C6-C8 and the canonical-section certificate depend on the certificate/divRep chain — take them as far as the frozen shapes allow and say plainly where you stopped.

ONE SCARE ALREADY CLOSED, do not re-open it: the GeometricallyReduced hypothesis at Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79 is REDUNDANT, not a gap — Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130/:140 supply it as instances and the module is in the import closure (record at Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210). That file also proves Smooth => GeometricallyReduced in mathlib generality and is flagged as an upstreaming candidate.

WORKSHEET-FIRST IS THE HOUSE RULE on this lane: w4-datc-worksheet.md governs, and where a node says WORKSHEET-FIRST the worksheet section is written or updated BEFORE the Lean.

CONCURRENCY IS BINDING. Four AJCR teams at once. Follow informal/protocol-concurrent-lanes.md exactly: private-index compare-and-swap ledger commits (never a bare git commit), and the mkdir lake mutex at /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock (DIRECTORY lock; never flock it).

COORDINATION. You consume the divRep endpoint from ajcr-divrep and the widened DivFamZar shape from ajcr-cert-r2 — but the point of this lane is that CHART-U and C9b are developable PARAMETRICALLY in those shapes, so do not idle waiting. State your assumed shape on the AJCR conversation thread and ask them to confirm or correct it. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild.

This is a headless, one-shot session: work the task's REAL objective as far
as you genuinely can, committing progress as you go, then finish with the
brief final report the skill specifies.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
148	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
281	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
282	  as **memory**.
283	
284	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
285	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
286	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
287	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
288	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
289	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
290	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
291	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
292	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
293	
294	## Resuming after an interruption
295	
296	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
297	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
298	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
299	
300	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
301	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
302	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
303	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
304	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
305	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
306	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
307	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
308	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
309	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
310	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
311	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
312	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
313	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
314	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
315	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
316	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
317	
318	## Final report (your last message)
319	
320	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
321	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
322	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
323	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
324	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
325	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
326	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
327	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
328	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
329	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
330	not by itself a reason to stop.
331	
332	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
333	
334	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,

2	name: horizon-start
3	description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
4	---
5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
23	```
24	
25	The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
26	like:
27	
28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
33	```
34	
35	For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:
36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.
40	- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.
43	
44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.
71	
72	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
73	interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
74	orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
75	stand before proposing work.
76	
77	One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
78	for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
79	`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
80	check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
81	resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
82	the run's original plan.)
83	
84	## Then, before you start
85	
86	- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
87	  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
88	- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
89	  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
90	  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
91	- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
92	  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
93	  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
94	  `horizon-inbox`.
95	
96	Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
97	smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
98	here.

218	### 7.3 §2's "one open experiment" was already answered, by this file's own sibling
219	
220	§2 closes with *"At `g ≥ 2` no witness has ever been exhibited… It is not acceptable to keep
221	planning without knowing which."* That question was settled in the **same round**:
222	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` **ADDENDUM 4** (commit `d7e8348ce`) is titled *"the on-stratum witness
223	EXISTS"*, and roadmap leaf `…ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done` carrying the sharp theorem.
224	
225	**The conclusion stands on ADDENDUM 4, not on what follows.** A ground review corrected the
226	first draft of this subsection, which claimed the argument below "agrees with" ADDENDUM 4 and holds
227	"over any field". It does neither. ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 uses the universal divisor over `Sym^g C`,
228	base-changes to an extension and pads by `(g−1)Q₀`, and states at `spec-dd-r.md:826` that no
229	rational-point hypothesis is used anywhere. What follows is a **different, cheaper witness** — a
230	pencil rather than `Sym^g` — with a side condition ADDENDUM 4 does not need:
231	
232	> For any `g ≥ 2`, take a pencil of degree `g` on `C` one of whose members is a divisor
233	> `E ≥ s₀ + s_∞` with `π(s₀) = 0`, `π(s_∞) = ∞`. Such an `E` exists: `ℓ(E) = 1 + ℓ(K − E)`, so any
234	> `E` with `s₀ + s_∞ ≤ E ≤ K'` for a canonical `K' ≥ s₀ + s_∞` has `ℓ(E) ≥ 2`; and such a `K'`
235	> exists because `ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2 ≥ 1` for `g ≥ 3`, and for `g = 2` exactly when `s_∞` is
236	> the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀` (which one is free to arrange, since `π` is a choice: a
237	> function with a zero at `s₀` and a pole at `s_∞` is a finite map sending them to `0` and `∞`).
238	> The support of the total family is an open subscheme of the irreducible `C`, hence irreducible,
239	> hence **connected after every Zariski shrink of the base** — which is exactly why the shrink
240	> evasion that kills the `g = 1` case does not apply here.

242	**The side condition, and it is not cosmetic.** Writing `s₀ + s_∞` and computing
243	`ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2` treats `s₀, s_∞` as *degree-1* points. Over a non-closed field the
244	minimal closed points `q₀ ∈ π⁻¹(0)`, `q₁ ∈ π⁻¹(∞)` have residue degrees `e₀, e₁`, and an effective
245	`E ≥ q₀ + q₁` of degree `g` exists only if **`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`**. Over `𝔽₂` with `g = 2` and
246	`e₀ = e₁ = 2` this witness does not exist — which is exactly the regime ADDENDUM 4 §4.4's
247	"only if" direction isolates. Secondly, the `g = 2` case above needs `π` chosen so that `s_∞` is
248	the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀`, whereas ADDENDUM 4 holds for any finite dominant `π`.
249

14	predicate is intrinsic to the *fibre class* of the datum.  Both are stated per datum.  This
15	file makes the step neither takes: it indexes the locus by a **class**.
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.cechWitnessLocus π c` — `{q : Spec B | every basic-open cocycle datum
18	  with fibre class `c` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` at `κ(q)`}`.
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum` — any ONE presenting datum is a
20	  sound and complete test (class-intrinsicity).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists` — the ∀-form and the ∃-form agree
22	  (every class is presented, `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`).
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_cechWitnessLocus` — the openness.
24	
25	## THIS IS NOT `chartLocus`, AND NOT `isOpen_chartLocus`
26	
27	Those two names are RESERVED, and co-signed between two lanes: `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md`
28	§3.3 (CHART-U(a)) freezes `chartLocus c λ` for a locus over a general test `T`, indexed by a
29	**plus class** `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, at the **twisted** fibre class
30	`λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)`; `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it with two binding
31	amendments — the predicate for arbitrary plus classes is the SPLIT form over a finite
32	separable `L/κ(t)`, and the openness route of record is a three-transport chain — and row B-4
33	owns `isOpen_chartLocus` as the *assembly* of DAT-B's transports (i)/(ii) against DAT-C's
34	shifted-datum half.  None of that is here.
35	
36	What IS here is the step those amendments presuppose and nobody had written: over an affine
37	base, for an UNTWISTED `CechPic` class, the engine's per-datum output is a locus of the class.
38	Call it transport (0).  Still missing for `chartLocus` proper: the shifted-datum constructor
39	(DAT-C GAP-1 — no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul`/tensor exists), the split predicate
40	(a-amendment), and transports (i) descent and (ii) étale image (DAT-B).
41	
42	Free of the DD-R certificate lane and of `divRep`: no `DivFamZar`, no `IsCertified`, no
43	`RepresentableBy` datum appears in the cone.
44	-/

61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
62	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

64	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
65	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

67	variable (π) in
68	/-- **The witness locus of an untwisted class over an affine base**: the set of points of
69	`Spec B` at which the fibre of the Čech class `c` admits an effective witness divisor with
70	vanishing `H¹`.
71	
72	Stated over *classes*, not over data: a basic-open cocycle datum is a presentation, and the
73	campaign's consumers index charts by a Picard class.  The ∀-quantifier is harmless because
74	the predicate is class-intrinsic
75	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`) and every class is
76	presented (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) — see
77	`mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
78	
79	NOT the co-signed `chartLocus c λ` of `w4-datc` §3.3 / `w4-datb` §1.6: that one lives over a
80	general test, is indexed by a plus class, and reads the TWISTED fibre class.  See the module
81	header. -/
82	def cechWitnessLocus (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B) :=
83	  {q : PrimeSpectrum B | ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
84	    D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField}
85	
86	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
87	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
88	      D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
89	  Iff.rfl
90	
91	/-- **Membership is testable at any one presentation**: a datum `D` presenting `c` is a
92	sound and complete test for membership of the witness locus.  This is the class-intrinsicity
93	of the witness predicate, `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, in the form
94	the consumers use. -/
95	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum {c : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
96	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hD : D.cechPicClass = c) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
97	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
98	  refine ⟨fun h => h D hD, fun h D' hD' => ?_⟩
99	  refine (D'.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq D
100	    q.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_).mpr h
101	  exact congrArg (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
102	    (hD'.trans hD.symm)
103	
104	/-- **The ∀-form and the ∃-form of the witness locus agree**: every class is presented by
105	some datum, and the witness predicate does not depend on which. -/
106	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
107	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
108	      D.cechPicClass = c ∧ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
109	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
110	  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨D₀, hD₀, h D₀ hD₀⟩, fun ⟨D, hD, h⟩ => ?_⟩
111	  exact (mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D hD q).mpr h
112	
113	/-- **The class-indexed witness locus is open**: it is the witness locus of any one
114	presenting datum, and that is open by
115	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` (the audited,
116	Noetherian-free openness engine).
117	
118	This is the first *datum-choice-free* openness statement in the campaign — the engine output
119	is stated for a chosen `D`, which is not something a locus indexed by a Picard class may
120	depend on.  It is strictly weaker than the reserved `isOpen_chartLocus` (dat-b row B-4),
121	which assembles this with the shifted-datum constructor and the descent/étale-image
122	transports; do not cite it as that. -/
123	theorem isOpen_cechWitnessLocus (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
124	    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : IsOpen (cechWitnessLocus π c) := by
125	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
126	  have hset : cechWitnessLocus π c
127	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
128	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
129	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
130	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
131	                    D₀.cechPicClass
132	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
133	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
134	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} :=
135	    Set.ext fun q => mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D₀ hD₀ q
136	  rw [hset]
137	  exact D₀.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
138	
139	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/

50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl

71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170

9	/-!
10	# The Abel chart map of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
11	
12	`JacobianData.ofCharts` consumes a family of morphisms of big-site presheaves
13	`yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C`.  This file builds such a morphism out of the two
14	things the tree already has: the Abel transformation of divisor families into the degree-zero
15	Picard functor on the slice, and a representation of the divisor functor by a scheme.
16	
17	The passage from the slice to the big site is the Σ-extension, and it is functorial in two
18	independent ways, both established here in the general categorical setting:
19	
20	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat` — the Σ-extension is functorial in the extended
21	  presheaf: a natural transformation `F ⟶ G` of presheaves on the slice `Over S` induces one
22	  of presheaves on the ambient category.
23	* `CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.toSigmaExtension` — a representation of `F` by an
24	  object `J` of the slice induces a morphism `yoneda.obj J.left ⟶ sigmaExtension S F` from the
25	  ambient yoneda presheaf of the underlying object.  A point of `J.left` over a test `V` is a
26	  map `v : V ⟶ J.left`, and it names the Σ-element whose structure morphism is `v ≫ J.hom` and
27	  whose fibre component is the universal element pulled back along `v`.
28	
29	Composing the second with the first at the Abel transformation gives the chart map.
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartValueTrans` — **the Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard
34	  functor**: under the chart-index degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value
35	  `abelDiv s · sigmaFamily Z · (θ^m)⁻¹` of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` is a natural transformation
36	  `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.  Naturality is `picEtMap_chartValue`, membership is
37	  `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChart` — **the Abel chart map**: given a representation of the
39	  divisor functor by a scheme `D` over `k` (a section variable — this file never constructs
40	  one), the morphism of big-site presheaves
41	  `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` sending a `D`-point to the class of the divisor
42	  family it names, twisted into degree zero.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_abelSigmaChart` — the structure morphism of the single chart of
44	  this family is the structure morphism of the representing object, so the chart hypothesis
45	  `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` of `JacobianData.ofCharts` is exactly
46	  `LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` for it.
47	
48	## What this is NOT
49	
50	This is the chart *map*, not a chart *atlas*.  Neither of the two properties
51	`JacobianData.ofCharts` needs is established here, and neither is available anywhere in the
52	tree today:
53	
54	* `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
55	  scheme** — the Abel map of a degree-`n` divisor scheme onto the Picard functor has projective
56	  spaces `|D|` as its fibres, so it is not a monomorphism, let alone an open immersion.  It
57	  becomes an open immersion only after restricting to the open locus where the fibre is a single
58	  point, i.e. where `h⁰ = 1`; that locus is the reserved `chartLocus` of `w4-datc` §3.3, which
59	  does not exist in Lean (see `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`, whose header states the
60	  remaining gaps).
61	* `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc …)` is the statement that
62	  every degree-zero class is Zariski-locally the twisted class of a divisor family in the
63	  window.  Over a field this is Riemann–Roch; the relative statement is DAT-B's coverage row.
64	-/
65	
66	set_option autoImplicit false
67	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
68	
69	universe v u
70	
71	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
72	
73	/-! ## Σ-extension plumbing (general category theory)
74	
75	Both constructions below are stated for presheaves valued in `Type v`, the hom-universe of the
76	ambient category, because that is where the ambient yoneda presheaf lives and the Σ-extension
77	must meet it. -/
78	
79	namespace CategoryTheory
80	
81	namespace Over
82	
83	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} {F G : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
84	
85	/-- **The Σ-extension is functorial in the extended presheaf**: a natural transformation of
86	presheaves on the slice induces one of their Σ-extensions, acting as the identity on the
87	structure-morphism component. -/
88	def sigmaExtensionNat (φ : F ⟶ G) : sigmaExtension S F ⟶ sigmaExtension S G where
89	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom fun x => ⟨x.1, φ.app _ x.2⟩
90	  naturality T T' g := by
91	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_
92	    obtain ⟨a, ξ⟩ := x
93	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk (g.unop ≫ a))
94	      (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (φ.naturality (Over.homMk g.unop rfl :
95	        Over.mk (g.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a).op) ξ)
96	
97	@[simp]
98	lemma sigmaExtensionNat_app_fst (φ : F ⟶ G) (T : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (sigmaExtension S F).obj T) :
99	    ((sigmaExtensionNat φ).app T x).1 = x.1 :=
100	  rfl
101	
102	end Over

104	namespace Functor.RepresentableBy

106	open Over
107	
108	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} {F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
109	
110	/-- The elementwise naturality identity behind `toSigmaExtension`, stated on the raw
111	Σ-extension transition function so that no bundled-hom coercion intervenes. -/
112	private lemma toSigmaExtension_aux {J : Over S} (α : F.RepresentableBy J)
113	    {T T' : C} (g : T' ⟶ T) (v : T ⟶ J.left) :
114	    (⟨(g ≫ v) ≫ J.hom, α.homEquiv (Over.homMk (g ≫ v) rfl)⟩ :
115	        Σ a : T' ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk a)))
116	      = Over.sigmaExtensionMap S F g ⟨v ≫ J.hom, α.homEquiv (Over.homMk v rfl)⟩ := by
117	  refine sigmaExtension_ext F (Category.assoc g v J.hom) ?_
118	  show F.map (mkCongr (Category.assoc g v J.hom)).op
119	      (F.map (Over.homMk g rfl :
120	        Over.mk (g ≫ (v ≫ J.hom)) ⟶ Over.mk (v ≫ J.hom)).op
121	        (α.homEquiv (Over.homMk v rfl))) = _
122	  rw [← Functor.map_comp_apply, ← op_comp, ← α.homEquiv_comp]
123	  refine congrArg α.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_)
124	  exact congrArg (fun z : T' ⟶ T => z ≫ v) (Category.id_comp g)
125	
126	/-- **The ambient presheaf map of a slice representation**: if `F` on the slice `Over S` is
127	represented by `J`, then the ambient yoneda presheaf of `J.left` maps to the Σ-extension of `F`.
128	A `V`-point `v : V ⟶ J.left` is sent to the Σ-element with structure morphism `v ≫ J.hom` and
129	fibre component the universal element restricted along `v`.
130	
131	This is the input shape of mathlib's 01JJ engine: a scheme mapping to a big-site presheaf. -/
132	def toSigmaExtension {J : Over S} (α : F.RepresentableBy J) :
133	    yoneda.obj J.left ⟶ sigmaExtension S F where
134	  app _ := TypeCat.ofHom fun v => ⟨v ≫ J.hom, α.homEquiv (Over.homMk v rfl)⟩
135	  naturality _ _ g :=
136	    ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun v => toSigmaExtension_aux α g.unop v
137	
138	@[simp]
139	lemma toSigmaExtension_app_fst {J : Over S} (α : F.RepresentableBy J) (T : Cᵒᵖ)
140	    (v : T.unop ⟶ J.left) :
141	    ((α.toSigmaExtension).app T v).1 = v ≫ J.hom :=
142	  rfl
143	
144	end Functor.RepresentableBy
145	
146	end CategoryTheory

148	/-! ## The Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard functor -/
149	
150	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
151	
152	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
153	
154	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
155	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
156	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
157	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
158	
159	noncomputable section
160	
161	variable (C π n) in
162	/-- **The Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard functor**: under the chart-index
163	degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` — the Abel class
164	of the divisor family, shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned
165	θ-family — is a natural transformation `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.
166	
167	The degree ledger of `degAt_chartValue` is what makes the target the degree-*zero* functor:
168	the three factors contribute `n`, `deg Z` and `−m·d₁`, which the constraint sums to zero. -/
169	def chartValueTrans (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
170	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
171	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
172	    divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C where
173	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom fun s => ⟨chartValue C π n m Z T.unop s,
174	    chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg T.unop s⟩
175	  naturality T T' g := by
176	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun s => ?_
177	    exact Subtype.ext ((picEtMap_chartValue C π n m Z g.unop s).symm)
178	
179	@[simp]
180	lemma chartValueTrans_app_coe (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
181	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
182	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
183	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
184	    ((chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg).app T s).1 = chartValue C π n m Z T.unop s :=
185	  rfl
186	
187	/-! ## The Abel chart map -/
188	
189	variable (C π n) in
190	/-- **The Abel chart map** of a representation of the divisor functor: the morphism of big-site
191	presheaves `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` sending a `D`-point to the degree-zero class
192	of the divisor family that point names.
193	
194	`rep` is a *hypothesis* — this file never constructs a representation of the divisor functor;
195	that is the divisor-representability obligation of the `DivRep…` lane.  Given one, this is the
196	Abel–Jacobi map at the level of the Σ-extension, and it is the only kind of object
197	`JacobianData.ofCharts` accepts. -/
198	def abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
199	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
200	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
201	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
202	    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
203	  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg)
204	
205	/-- **The structure morphism of the Abel chart is that of the representing object**: for the
206	one-element family consisting of the Abel chart map, the chart structure morphism `chartHom`
207	that `JacobianData.ofCharts` reads off is `D.hom` itself.
208	
209	So the finiteness hypotheses of the producer, specialised to this chart, are exactly
210	`LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` and `CompactSpace D.left` — properties of the divisor scheme, with
211	no reference to the Picard functor. -/
212	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
213	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
214	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
215	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
216	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
217	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
218	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) i = D.hom :=
219	  Category.id_comp _
220	
221	end
222	
223	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) gap-2, the chartLocus-free core — fibre-field invariance of witness
10	h¹-vanishing (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 transport (ii), I-0252 gap 2)
11	
12	CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii) (the "one `IsOpenMap` application", `Pic0ChartLocusOpen`
13	keystones 2/3) pushes the engine's open witness locus from the étale carrier `Spec B`
14	down to the test base `Spec A`.  Its remaining mathematical content (I-0252 gap 2) is
15	the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the preimage of the base locus with the
16	carrier locus: for a prime `q` of the carrier over `p`, the residue-field extension
17	`κ(q)/κ(p)` is separable (étale/étale-plus carrier) and must **preserve** the witness
18	h¹-vanishing of the fibre class.
19

81	/-! ## The module-theoretic core -/
82	
83	/-- **Base change of a module along a field extension preserves triviality**: for an
84	`S`-module `H` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is
85	subsingleton iff `H ⊗[S] L'` is.
86	
87	Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the (nonzero) field
88	extension `L → L'` (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality`), read across the
89	base-change-in-stages equivalence `(TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange)`.
90	**Separability is not used** — every field extension is faithfully flat. -/
91	theorem subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
92	    {S L L' H : Type u} [CommRing S] [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra S L] [Algebra S L']
93	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower S L L'] [AddCommGroup H] [Module S H] :
94	    Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L) ↔ Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L') := by
95	  have e := TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange S L L' L' H
96	  rw [(TensorProduct.comm S H L).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
97	      (TensorProduct.comm S H L').toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
98	      ← e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr]
99	  exact ⟨fun _ => inferInstance,
100	    fun _ => Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality L L' (L ⊗[S] H)⟩
101	
102	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

109	
110	/-- **The chart-membership witness predicate at a field `L`** — the field-parametrised
111	form of the set of `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
112	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`): the fibre class of `D` at `L` admits an effective witness divisor
113	with vanishing `H¹`.  For `L = q.asIdeal.ResidueField` this is definitionally membership
114	of `q` in the keystone-1 witness locus. -/
115	def BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
116	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [IsScalarTower k B L] : Prop :=
117	  ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
118	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
119	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
120	      ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
121	
122	/-- The witness predicate is the engine's complex-form fibre condition
123	`Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)`, via the two-way datum dictionary
124	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6). -/
125	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton
126	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
127	    [IsScalarTower k B L] :
128	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L) :=
129	  (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness L).symm
130	
131	/-! ## The fibre-field invariance (the gap-2 core) -/
132	
133	/-- **CHART-U(b) gap-2 core — fibre-field invariance of witness h¹-vanishing**: for a
134	pinned datum `D` over the affine base `B` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the
135	`k`/`B` tower (the residue-field seam `κ(p) → κ(q)` of a carrier map `comap f`), the
136	witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'`.
137	
138	Both sides are, via the datum dictionary, `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] ·)`, and
139	that transfers along the (faithfully flat) field extension `L → L'`
140	(`subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff`).  In particular this covers the separable
141	residue-field extensions of an étale/étale-plus carrier map. -/
142	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
143	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
144	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
145	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
146	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] :
147	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' := by
148	  rw [D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L,
149	      D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L']
150	  exact subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
151	
152	/-- **The separable specialisation the CHART-U(b) transport (ii) names** (I-0252 gap 2):
153	for a **separable** residue-field extension `L → L'` (`Algebra.IsSeparable`, the case of
154	an étale/étale-plus carrier map), witness h¹-vanishing of `D` transfers between `L` and
155	`L'`.  Separability is recorded to name the intended consumer; the transfer holds for any
156	field extension (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`). -/
157	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable
158	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
159	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
160	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
161	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] :
162	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' :=
163	  D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension L L'
164	
165	/-! ## Fixed-field class-intrinsicity (the other half the `comap` identity needs) -/
166	
167	/-- **Class-intrinsicity of the witness predicate at a fixed field** (V1a): the witness
168	h¹-vanishing predicate depends only on the mapped fibre class
169	`Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass`, so two data — over possibly
170	different bases `B`, `B'` — whose fibre classes at `L` agree have the same witness
171	predicate at `L`.
172	
173	Together with `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` (the `κ(p) → κ(q)` transfer)
174	this is exactly what the CHART-U(b) `comap`-preimage identity reduces to at C9-time; the
175	one residual input is the shifted-datum class identity of I-0252 gap 1 (the Σ/θ
176	naturality), which is divRep-gated. -/
177	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq
178	    {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B']
179	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (D' : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B' π)
180	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra B' L]
181	    [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B' L]
182	    (hcl : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
183	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B' L) D'.cechPicClass) :
184	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D'.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
185	  simp only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hcl]

9	# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
10	(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)
11	
12	The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
13	basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.
14	
15	For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
16	fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
17	is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
18	campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
19	through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
20	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
21	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
22	condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
23	pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.
24	
25	Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):
26	
27	* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
28	  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
29	  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
30	  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
31	  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
32	  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
33	* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
34	  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
35	  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
36	  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
37	  invariance identifies the preimage.
38	
39	The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
40	(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
41	-/

131	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap

/-!
# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)

For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The degree at a field point -/

/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))

section DegAt

variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
@[simp]
theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]

/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]

/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
  rfl

/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
  rw [← picEtMap_comp]

/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

end DegAt

/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
    degAt lam t = 0}
  one_mem' := by
    intro K _ _ t
    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro a ha K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
          degAt lam t = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

variable (C) in
/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
points. -/
def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))

/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
@[simp]
theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
functor. -/
def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
  map_id T := by
    ext lam U
    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
  map_comp g h := by
    ext lam U
    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
